Jurisdictional Highway System Plan
In addition, SEWRPC has refined and detailed the initial regional surface transportation plan as it pertains to Milwaukee County. SEWRPC has recommended the jurisdictional responsibility for the construction, maintenance, and operation for each segment of artieral streets and highways in Milwaukee County. This study, in cooperation with federal, state and all concerned local units of government proceeded with the conversion of the functional highway plan contained within the adopted regional transportation plan to a Jurisdictional Highway System Plan. See figure 7.
Since the adoption of this plan by the governmental agencies involved, it is being used by Milwaukee County as a basis for improvements of arterial streets and highways within Milwaukee County. Implementing the plan should provide the County with an integrated highway transportation system which would promote desirable land use patterns, abate traffic congestion, reduce accidents and travel times.
The Jurisdictional Highway System Plan was adopted by the Milwaukee County Board in January 1970, and the communities of St. Francis, Cudahy, and Oak Creek on January 6, 1970, October 21, 1969, and February 17, 1970, respectively.
This plan specifically recommends that General Mitchell Field be connected to Interstate Route I-94 by a four-lane divided freeway. This would fulfill the basic warrants as adopted in this study for highway service to a major traffic generator.
The initial regional surface transportation plan investigated and discussed all forms of alternative modes of transportation including fixed rail in order to provide a balanced system for the region.
